note:
FOR campaign/census-tail -- YOUR CENSUS RAN GREEN AND MOVED NO GOLDENS. That is the important half: a parallelism change that altered any output would have been a determinism finding, and it altered none. rc=0 in 1211 s, delivery branch carries the timings row only.

THE PERF NUMBER, HOWEVER, DOES NOT DEMONSTRATE AN IMPROVEMENT, and I would rather tell you that than hand you a favourable-looking total.

                                total  studies   tail  tail user  ratio
    baseline A (the-lot)       1278.2    970.2  307.9     2267.1   7.36
    baseline B (the-lot)       1186.0    964.9  221.2      985.5   4.46
    yours                      1197.5    949.9  247.6     1058.2   4.27

Your tail of 247.6 s sits INSIDE the baseline range [221.2, 307.9]. Those two baselines are the SAME TREE 51 minutes apart, so their 86.8 s spread is pure run-to-run noise, and your delta from their mean is 16.9 s. At n=1 the instrument cannot separate your change from the noise in either direction. This is not a null result; it is an UNRESOLVED one, which is a different and less useful thing.

TWO SECONDARY READINGS, offered as observations rather than conclusions:

  - the tail's cpu_ratio went 7.36 -> 4.46 -> 4.27. If "overlap census readout generation" increased parallelism you would expect that to rise. It did not. Ratio is noisy too, so this is weak evidence, but it is weak evidence in the wrong direction and worth explaining before claiming a win.
  - your STUDIES came in at 949.9 s against 970.2 and 964.9. A readout-generation change should not touch study wall at all, so that 15-20 s is either box variability or your change reaching further than intended. Worth a look: it is the control that is supposed to hold still.

WHAT I THINK THE REAL BLOCKER IS, and it is upstream of your change rather than a criticism of it. THE TAIL IS UNTIMED INTERNALLY. scripts/timed.sh wraps exactly three things — the two studies and the whole census — so the tail exists only as a subtraction, and the only way to measure any change inside it is by differencing totals whose noise is 87 s. Nobody can demonstrate a 20 s win that way, however real it is.

So the higher-value move is probably to instrument the tail's segments FIRST — the 747 SVG renders, the domesday survey, the anomaly report, the CSV writes — and then optimise against a measurement that can see the effect. That also settles the question my own attribution left open: I inferred the SVGs are the tail from artifact counts, and inference is all anyone has had so far.

If you want to keep the change on its own merits it needs three or four runs to clear the noise, which is 20 minutes of a serial box each. Instrumenting first is cheaper and answers more.
